subject: EU VAT handling for July invoice — reverse charge and GST split
messages:
From: Lauren Price <lauren.price@brightware.co.uk>
To: michael.grant@redwoodinference.com
Cc: accounts@brightware.co.uk
Date: 2026-08-01T09:12:00+01:00
Subject: Question about VAT treatment on July invoice (reverse charge)

Hi Michael,

Thanks again for the quick demo last week. Finance is reconciling our July invoices and we've hit a VAT question we hoped you could clarify. We received invoice_20260730.pdf for Redwood's hosting + support — total GBP 28,500. Because we're a UK-registered business buying services from a US-headquartered vendor with EU operations, our team thinks this should be treated under the reverse-charge mechanism (BrightWare to account for VAT) but we need Redwood to confirm the invoice layout and provide your VAT/registration information so our accounting team can reclaim correctly.

Specific asks:
- Please confirm Redwood's VAT registration number used on this invoice (or confirm reverse-charge applies and the invoice should be net).
- If reverse-charge applies, can you provide a short statement on the invoice or a supporting VAT certificate for our records?
- If part of the services are delivered to an APAC entity (we have a small support seat used from Singapore) we may need a split invoice for VAT vs GST. Can Redwood issue split invoices / self-billing if needed?

We are on a tight close timeline — would appreciate confirmation by EOD Wednesday.

Thanks,
Lauren Price
Finance Lead — BrightWare Ltd
[Attachment: purchase_order_BW-9987.pdf (PDF, 34KB)]

From: michael.grant@redwoodinference.com
To: Lauren Price <lauren.price@brightware.co.uk>
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-08-02T10:08:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Question about VAT treatment on July invoice (reverse charge)

Hi Lauren — thanks for the clear note and the PO.

Short answer: reverse charge is likely appropriate for the UK entity purchasing digital hosting/services from Redwood (US HQ) assuming BrightWare has a valid UK VAT registration and the place of supply is the UK. We can support both: a) annotate the existing invoice to call out "reverse charge — customer to account for VAT" plus Redwood's EUID/VAT-like identifier, or b) produce a split invoice if you confirm a portion should be charged to BrightWare Singapore (GST).

Next steps from our side:
- Vanessa (finance ops) will validate and attach Redwood's EU tax identifier and an explanatory note for the invoice.
- Laura (billing) — can you confirm whether BrightWare wants us to reissue a split invoice (UK net + Singapore billed amount) or just annotate the current invoice for reverse charge?
- If you elect split invoicing, please confirm the GBP / SGD allocation and provide the Singapore entity name/UTR you want on the invoice.

I don't expect legal sign-off for this; it's a standard cross-border VAT handling. We'll attach a short certificate (stub) so your AP team has evidence.

Best,
Michael Grant
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwoodinference.com
Cell: +44 7700 900111

[Attachment: Redwood_tax_identifier.txt (text, 2KB)]

From: vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com
To: michael.grant@redwoodinference.com, Lauren Price <lauren.price@brightware.co.uk>
Cc: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-08-04T14:20:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Question about VAT treatment on July invoice (reverse charge)

Hi all — looping in billing & collections.

Lauren — quick notes from finance ops: we can support two operational flows depending on what BrightWare prefers:

1) Annotated single invoice (fastest): we reissue invoice_20260730.pdf with the following line added: "Reverse charge — recipient to account for VAT under Article 199 (place of supply: UK). Redwood is not charging VAT on this supply." We'll include our tax registration string and a short signature block for audit. This is recommended if all services are being used by the UK entity.

2) Split invoice (required if a material portion of services were consumed by BrightWare Singapore): we'll generate two invoices — one net GBP to BrightWare Ltd (UK) and one invoice to BrightWare Singapore with GST applied according to Singapore rules. For split invoices we need: Singapore company name, UEN/VAT number, and the exact allocation (GBP/SGD amounts). Note: split invoices increase processing time (1–2 business days) and may trigger self-billing checks on both sides.

Evidence we require to treat this as reverse-charge (please upload to the Drive link):
- BrightWare UK VAT registration (VAT number + certificate).
- Confirmation that the service location is the UK (billing address + point of use).

Ben from collections: if BrightWare confirms reverse charge and uploads VAT evidence, can collections lift the invoice hold and proceed with net collection?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Finance Operations
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_tax_identifier.txt (text, 2KB)]

From: Lauren Price <lauren.price@brightware.co.uk>

Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: Question about VAT treatment on July invoice (reverse charge)

Thanks Michael and Vanessa — appreciate the prompt responses. BrightWare confirms the following today: 

- BrightWare Ltd (UK) VAT: GB123456789 — certificate attached.
- Services used by UK entity only; Singapore usage negligible.
- Please reissue the July invoice with the reverse-charge annotation and Redwood's tax identifier. We do not need a split invoice.

I've attached the VAT certificate and the PO for reference. If you can reissue the annotated invoice and confirm we should proceed with net payment to the existing account details, we'll release payment within our standard terms.

Best,
Lauren Price
Finance Lead — BrightWare Ltd
